How to read this. Each case opens with the run AICA actually performed, then the services it ranked and the content it planned, each with the reason behind the score. Setup values, authored expectations and raw records sit in collapsed panels underneath. These verdicts express fitness against an authored simulator hypothesis - they are not a safety certification, a medical judgement, or a claim about the physical world.

Rest behaviour

TC-R01

Protect a sleep-deprived late-shift worker with an early rest proposal

Partly appropriate; review details

睡眠不足の遅番勤務者を早めの休憩提案で守る

A logistics worker slept poorly during the day, completed a physically demanding late shift, and starts driving after only a brief pause. They must drive home at night on the Tokyo–Osaka expressway, where the first mapped service area is the practical stopping option. Drowsiness is 85 and fatigue is 70 at departure; the neutral profile contributes no preference or recovery-history shortcut. Both signals continue rising on the dark, uninterrupted highway before the first reachable rest area.

What AICA didrest_required at 141 min
Service offeredhumming_karaoke
Content plan5 tracks
Peak score0.715 / 0.70

TC-R03

Recognize post-shift exhaustion even before strong sleepiness appears

Partly appropriate; review details

強い眠気が出る前でも勤務後の消耗を認識する

A warehouse supervisor has been standing and coordinating urgent work for twelve hours but was not awake overnight. They take the night expressway home after the extended shift because public transport has ended. Fatigue starts at 78 while drowsiness is only 35; no service preference or recovery history competes with the physical-state evidence. TC-R06

Avoid an unactionable early proposal while the next rest stop is still distant (contrast with test case ID TC-R05)

Not appropriate for this hypothesis

次の休憩所がまだ遠い間は実行不能な早期提案を避ける（TC-R05との対照）

The same night courier begins with the same moderate drowsiness and fatigue after the same delivery workload. They instead take the long Tokyo–Osaka route, where the router-owned first service area remains substantially farther away. Drowsiness is 62 and fatigue 58 with the same growth, profile, and automatic service choice as TC-R05. The driver accumulates risk while the next mapped stopping opportunity is still distant, making an immediate stop instruction hard to execute.

Interrupt automatic driving on a familiar featureless night commute

Appropriate for this hypothesis

慣れた特徴のない夜間通勤で自動化した運転を中断する

An experienced commuter is physically rested but has driven the same expressway home hundreds of times. They drive the mostly-highway Tokyo–Chichibu route home late at night after routine desk work. Drowsiness and fatigue both start at 5, and the neutral history profile adds no recovery preference. After the early rest point is passed, a long familiar and visually repetitive highway section continues with only a brief early slowdown.

TC-M02

Avoid treating a first drive on the same route as habitual monotony (contrast with test case ID TC-M01)

Appropriate for this hypothesis

同じルートの初回走行を習慣的な単調さと扱わない（TC-M01との対照）

A rested driver is covering a colleague's shift and has never used this expressway route before. They drive the same mostly-highway Tokyo–Chichibu route at the same night hour as TC-M01. Drowsiness and fatigue both start at 5 with the same neutral profile; only route familiarity is removed. The road is still long and dark, but active navigation and novel landmarks keep it from being an automatic habitual drive.

TC-E02

Prefer non-distracting support for an exhausted worker crossing a mountain pass

Not appropriate for this hypothesis

峠を越える消耗した勤務者に注意を奪わない支援を優先する

A utility worker finishes emergency outdoor repairs after a long day and starts the return trip without a proper recovery break. They must cross the Tokyo–Karuizawa mountain corridor at night to return the service vehicle. Fatigue is 82 and drowsiness 68; the neutral profile deliberately contributes no entertainment preference. The painted 20–120 km mountain range adds winding-road workload while both physical signals continue to climb.

TC-E06

Choose rest over entertainment when severe fatigue and monotony coexist

Partly appropriate; review details

重い疲労と単調さが共存するとき娯楽より休憩を選ぶ

A driver begins after a double shift and has also driven the same featureless route for years. They attempt the long familiar night highway home, passing an early rest point before the repetitive section. Drowsiness is 88 and fatigue 86, while familiar-route and night monotony signals are also present. Severe physical risk and prolonged monotony compete from the start of the highway journey.

Content personalisation

TC-P01

Personalize an alertness playlist with the driver’s registered OSHI artist

Appropriate for this hypothesis

登録済み推しアーティストで覚醒プレイリストをパーソナライズする

A J-rock listener has registered synthetic-artist-0068 as their OSHI artist and explicitly enabled OSHI mode before departure. They drive the shared long familiar night highway home after an evening event. Physical signals start at 5; supported music and humming services have strong shared history, while radio_style is deliberately weak. Monotony builds after the early rest point, causing a supported alertness-audio service to request content.

Service offeredmusic_playlist
Content plan5 tracks

Build a preference-based playlist when OSHI mode is off (contrast with test case ID TC-P01)

Appropriate for this hypothesis

Avoid replaying a favorite song heard twenty minutes ago

Partly appropriate; review details

20分前に聴いたお気に入り曲の再生を避ける

Exclude a song the driver skipped moments ago

Appropriate for this hypothesis

運転者が数分前にスキップした曲を除外する

A listener usually favors synthetic-track-0058 but skipped it at 2026-07-29T11:55:00Z, five minutes before the reference time. At 2026-07-29T12:00:00Z they begin the same long familiar night-highway journey. Physical signals start at 5 and supported-service history is strong; the recent skip is the only negative item operation. The fixed skip remains current when monotony later requests a supported content plan.

Persuade a rest-averse worker rushing home to stop safely

Partly appropriate; review details

帰宅を急ぎ休憩を嫌う勤務者に安全な停車を促す

A restaurant manager finishes a double closing shift and wants to get home quickly, usually preferring audio support over stopping. They start the long night expressway home with a reachable mapped service area ahead. Drowsiness is 82 and fatigue 72; supported audio has good history, but physical risk is severe. Both signals rise as the worker presses on, so entertainment alone cannot make continued driving safe.

TC-I03

Break automatic driving before congestion on a familiar commute

Partly appropriate; review details

慣れた通勤路の渋滞前に自動化した運転を中断する

A physically rested office worker has driven the same night commute for years and uses no strongly preferred recovery service. They head home on the long familiar highway with congestion painted across km 110–170. Drowsiness and fatigue begin at 5; familiarity and forecast congestion, not exhaustion, define the risk story. A long repetitive stretch leads toward a 35-minute low-speed congestion period beginning after 55 minutes.

TC-I04

Restore attention for a mentally preoccupied commuter on a repetitive route

Appropriate for this hypothesis

反復ルートで考え事をする通勤者の注意を回復する

A rested commuter leaves work thinking intensely about a difficult meeting and has no service history to predetermine the intervention. They drive the long familiar and repetitive night highway home. Drowsiness and fatigue start at 5; mental preoccupation is narrative context because the simulator has no direct preoccupation input. After the early rest point, uninterrupted familiar-road exposure creates executable monotony while the commuter remains physically rested.

TC-I06

Energize a J-rock fan on the highway to a concert without confusing monotony with exhaustion

Not appropriate for this hypothesis

コンサートへ向かうJ-rockファンを消耗と混同せず高速道路で活性化する

A well-rested J-rock fan has a concert scheduled soon and a strong supported-music recovery history. They drive a long repetitive daytime expressway to the concert venue. Drowsiness and fatigue both start at 5; J-rock genre affinity and the concert schedule shape content but not trigger severity. The early rest point passes and prolonged highway repetition accumulates while the driver remains physically rested.
